newsitem.title: USA: Calif. panel OKs ban on insurer contributions.
newsitem.headline: Calif. panel OKs ban on insurer contributions.

text.p: A California legislative committee approved a bill that would bar the insurance industry from contributing to the office of the state insurance commissioner, state officials said Thursday.
Senate Bill 1097, introduced by Senator Quentin Kopp, was approved by the state Senate's Elections and Reapportionment Committee on a vote of 3-1.
It now advances to the Senate Appropriations Committee, Kopp's office said.

The bill would prohibit companies regulated by the state's insurance commissioner, their lobbyists and attorneys from making campaign contributions to the commissioner and candidates seeking that office.
The legislation would impose civil penalties of $5,000 to $10,000 for the first and second offenses. Repeat offenders could be disqualified from holding the elected office.
The bill was prompted in part by the campaign finance controversy surrounding the current state insurance commissioner, Chuck Quackenbush.
Campaign committees controlled by Quackenbush have received millions of dollars from insurance industry sources since 1994, according to watchdog groups.
Last month, Quackenbush agreed to pay a $50,000 fine for alleged violations of state campaign contribution disclosure rules during his 1994 campaign.
Quackenbush's campaign committee had no immediate comment on the bill. The state's Department of Insurance said it has not taken a position on the proposed legislation.
